_comment: Held-out evaluation set. Written by independent authors who saw only the article and the seed corpus; every label confirmed by a blind second annotator (disagreements dropped). 'dev' is the only split thresholds may be tuned on; 'test' is reported. Red-team items are all 'test'. See novelty/evaluation.py.

items.label: novel
items.headline: My wheelchair van needs a real space, not a shuttle
items.body: I use a power wheelchair and drive a side-entry van. The Elm Street garage is the only place downtown where I can reliably find a van-accessible bay with enough room beside it to lower my ramp. Street spaces on Main are parallel, sloped and right up against traffic, so getting out there means rolling into a live lane. A long walk or a bus ride from an outer lot is not a small thing for me, and nobody has said whether the promised shuttle will even have a lift or wheelchair tie-downs. The article doesn't mention disabled residents at all. Before the garage comes down, the council should tell us exactly where the accessible spaces are going, how many there will be, and whether they will be close enough to the shops, the pharmacy and the bank to actually be usable.

items.label: novel
items.headline: ppl gonna park on OUR street now
items.body: i live on birch st, 2 blocks from the garage. when theres a game or event our street is already packed w cars from downtown. take away 600 spots and every shopper n office worker is gonna circle our block all day lookin for a space. council shud do resident permit parking on the side streets b4 they knock it down or we wont be able to park at our own houses

items.label: novel
items.headline: Has anyone actually counted how full the garage is?
items.body: I walk past the Elm Street garage every morning on my way to work and the top three levels are close to empty most days, full only for the holiday parade and the odd concert. Before we argue about losing 600 spaces, the city should publish its own occupancy counts by hour and by day. If peak use is really 250 cars, the loss is a lot smaller than the shop owners fear, and cheaper fixes may cover it.

items.label: novel
items.headline: What about EV charging?
items.body: Downtown's only public EV chargers are in that garage.

items.label: novel
items.headline: nothing in this park for teenagers
items.body: every body keeps talking about playgrounds for little kids but what about teenagers?? my son is 15 and theres no where downtown for him and his freinds to go that isnt a store where they get told to leave. put in a basket ball court or even just some covered tables where teens are aloud to hang out. otherwise they will be the ones blamed when the park 'attracts trouble'.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Bathrooms, please
items.body: Without public restrooms, families won't stay long.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Build a playground my daughter can use too
items.body: My daughter uses a wheelchair, and most playgrounds are a bed of wood chips she can't cross, with equipment she can't reach. If Riverton is building from scratch, make it an inclusive playground: rubber surfacing, ramps up to the play decks, wheelchair swings and a quiet sensory corner for kids who get overwhelmed. It costs a bit more up front, but it's the only kind of playground every family downtown could actually use.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Read the fine print on those state grants
items.body: State green-space grants usually come with a spending deadline and a local match requirement. If demolition slips a year, as these things do, the city could miss the window and either return the money or cover the gap from the general fund. I'd like to know what happens to the $14 million plan if the grant share disappears in 2027.

items.label: novel
items.headline: The garage makes money we'd be giving up
items.body: People forget the city collects fees at that garage every single day. Between hourly tickets and event parking it has to bring in a decent sum each year, and I'd bet some of it goes toward street repairs or the downtown budget. Nobody has said how that income gets replaced once the garage is gone, and the lost revenue should be counted as part of the park's real cost.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Compare the park to what fixing the garage would cost
items.body: Everyone is treating $14 million as if the alternative costs nothing. It doesn't. That garage went up decades ago, and anyone who parks on the third level has seen the rust stains, the exposed rebar and the flakes of concrete coming off the ceiling. Structures that age usually need a major rehabilitation: new waterproofing, new expansion joints, sometimes a whole deck replaced, and that bill alone can run into the millions. If the honest choice is between spending $14 million on a park and spending eight or ten million just to keep a crumbling garage standing for another twenty years, the park looks very different. The council should publish the most recent structural inspection so we can compare the real options, instead of comparing a park to an imaginary free garage.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Young trees won't cool anything until the 2040s
items.body: The heat argument assumes shade, but a newly planted tree takes fifteen or twenty years to cast a real canopy. If the city plants saplings in 2028, the kids who play there now will be grown before it's any cooler. Either budget for large, mature trees from the start or put up shade sails and pergolas to cover the gap years.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Who waters two acres in a drought?
items.body: Heat waves usually come with watering restrictions. A big lawn that turns brown and bare in August doesn't cool much of anything, and keeping it green would take thousands of gallons of treated drinking water. Plant drought-tolerant native grasses and shrubs instead of turf and use drip irrigation for the trees.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Better make city bus free than new shuttle
items.body: Why make a new shuttle from far lot when we have already bus lines going to downtown? Better the council pay so the city buses is free for ride to downtown during all the construction. Then people come direct from they own neighborhood, not drive first to parking lot and wait. I think is more cheap than new shuttle, and it help also the people who not have car.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Let shops reward people who ride the shuttle
items.body: If the shuttle is going to work, give people a reason to take it. Main Street merchants could offer 10 percent off to anyone who shows a shuttle ticket, the way some stores validate parking. The chamber of commerce could run it, and it would turn the shuttle from a hassle into a small perk.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Start a Friends of Elm Street Park group
items.body: The upkeep worry is fair, but it doesn't all have to land on the parks department. Plenty of cities have a nonprofit conservancy that raises donations, organizes volunteer weeding days and lets local businesses adopt a flower bed. If a friends group were set up before opening day, the park would have people with a real stake in keeping it nice.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Busy parks are safe parks
items.body: Cameras and patrols help, but what really keeps a park safe after dark is ordinary people using it. Put in a coffee kiosk that stays open until 9, schedule evening fitness classes and outdoor movie nights, and face the benches toward the paths. When there are always people around, trouble tends to move on by itself.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Design the park to soak up Elm Street's floodwater
items.body: Every heavy storm, the corner of Elm and Third turns into a lake because the garage and the streets around it dump all their runoff straight into old storm drains. Two acres of soil can absorb a lot of that if it's built with rain gardens, a sunken lawn and permeable paths. That could save the city money on drain upgrades and keep downtown basements dry.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Where will the people sleeping in the stairwells go?
items.body: On cold nights I count six or seven people sleeping in the Elm Street garage stairwells, out of the wind. I work the early shift at the bakery across the street and a couple of them I know by name. When the garage comes down, those people aren't going to vanish. They'll end up in doorways on Main Street, which is exactly what the shop owners say they're afraid of. I'm not against the park. I'm asking the council to put money for outreach workers and shelter beds into the project plan now, and to have caseworkers talk to the people staying there months before the demolition crews show up, instead of sending police the week of. Doing it that way is kinder, and it works better for everyone downtown, housed or not.

items.label: novel
items.headline: A nicer downtown could price out the people who live there
items.body: I rent a one-bedroom two blocks from the garage, and I've been reading about what happened in other cities after big new parks opened. Property values next to them jumped, landlords raised rents, and a lot of the long-time tenants and the cheap little businesses, the laundromat, the barber, the corner grocery, got pushed out within a few years. The people the park was supposedly for couldn't afford to live beside it any more. I like the park idea, but I want the council to pair it with protections: limits on rent increases for existing tenants near the site, or help for small commercial tenants when their leases come up. Otherwise we're building a lovely backyard for whoever moves in next.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Any conflicts of interest?
items.body: Which council members own buildings facing the new park?

items.label: novel
items.headline: Put the comment form in Spanish too
items.body: A lot of the families in the apartments around Elm Street speak Spanish or Vietnamese at home. If the only way to comment before October 31 is an English form on the city website, they're effectively shut out. Translate the notice, leave paper copies at the grocery stores and the church, and hold at least one meeting with interpreters.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Room for bikes
items.body: Include secure bike racks so people can cycle there.

items.label: novel
items.headline: theres falcons nesting on that garage!!
items.body: not joking, a pair of peregrine falcons has nested on the top deck of the elm st garage for like 3 yrs now, the birdwatching club tracks them. if they demolish in spring they wreck the nest n its probably illegal too. pls do the demo outside nesting season and put a nest box up on a tall building nearby so they stay downtown

items.label: novel
items.headline: Demolishing sound concrete is not climate-friendly
items.body: Supporters keep calling this a climate decision, but tearing down thousands of tons of concrete throws away all the carbon that went into making it, and new walls, paths and play equipment add more. It would take decades of tree growth to make that back. If the council wants climate credit, it should publish a carbon estimate for the demolition, not just count the trees.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Keep the lower levels, put the park on the roof
items.body: Why does it have to be all or nothing? Other cities have turned the top of a parking structure into a garden. Keep the two lower levels for short-term shopper parking and build the green space on the roof deck and around the base. We'd keep a few hundred spaces and still get a park.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Save a wall for local artists
items.body: Riverton has plenty of talented muralists and sculptors who never get public commissions. Set aside one percent of the budget for art made by people from here: a mural along the north wall, a few sculptures kids can climb on. It would give the park its own identity instead of looking like every other catalog green space.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Think about the people who work downtown too
items.body: Most of the talk is about residents and shoppers, but there are hundreds of us in the office buildings around Elm Street who eat lunch at our desks because there's nowhere to sit outside. Movable chairs, tables in the shade, a few power outlets and decent Wi-Fi would fill the park at noon every weekday.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Riverton Elementary could use this as a classroom
items.body: The downtown elementary school has a fenced asphalt yard and no garden at all. If the park had a small outdoor classroom, a few rows of log seats, a pond or a vegetable bed, teachers could walk their classes over for science lessons. Ask the school district to help design that corner now, not after it's built.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Set targets now and report back every year
items.body: Supporters say the park will bring foot traffic, opponents say it will kill sales. Both sides are guessing. The council should count pedestrians and track sales tax receipts on Main Street this year, before demolition, and publish the same numbers every year after the park opens. If the results are bad, the data will show what needs fixing.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Kids will be crossing a busy street to get there
items.body: Elm Street is four lanes and people drive it like a highway. Right now nobody tries to cross it with a toddler. Once there's a playground on one side and apartments on the other, they will. The plan needs raised crosswalks, a lower speed limit and maybe a signal before the park opens, not after the first accident.

items.label: seq_first
items.headline: Aim the park lights down, not into our bedrooms
items.body: I live on the fourth floor facing the garage. When the park gets its safety lighting, please use shielded fixtures that point at the ground. Tall floodlights would shine straight into every apartment along Elm Street all night and wash out the stars too.

items.label: seq_second
items.headline: Shield the lamps so neighbors can sleep
items.body: Whatever lamps go up around the new green, pick hooded ones with a downward beam. My flat overlooks that site, and glaring poles would pour brightness through our windows until dawn and ruin any view of the night sky.

items.label: seq_first
items.headline: Add a pick-up and drop-off lane
items.body: Losing the garage makes a proper curbside zone for taxis, ride-share cars and delivery vans more important. Mark a short loading lane on Elm Street next to the park so drivers can stop for two minutes without double-parking and blocking traffic.

items.label: seq_second
items.headline: Give Uber and couriers a spot to pull over
items.body: With fewer places to leave a car, more folks will be dropped off by app drivers, and parcels still have to arrive somehow. Paint a brief stopping bay beside the green where a cab or van can idle for a moment instead of halting in the middle of the road.

items.label: seq_first
items.headline: Put solar panels on the park pavilion
items.body: If the park is getting a shelter or pavilion, cover its roof with solar panels. They could power the path lighting and the drinking fountains, cut the running costs, and show kids how renewable energy works.

items.label: seq_second
items.headline: Let the sun pay the park's electric bill
items.body: Any covered structure built on the site should carry photovoltaic modules on top. The electricity they generate could run the lamps and pumps, trim what the city spends each year on utilities, and double as a hands-on lesson in clean power for schoolchildren.

items.label: seq_first
items.headline: Let restaurants put tables out facing the park
items.body: The city should make it easy for cafés and restaurants across from the park to get outdoor seating permits. Diners would love eating next to the green space, and it would help the same businesses worried about losing garage parking.

items.label: seq_second
items.headline: Sidewalk dining should come with the green
items.body: Fast-track licenses for eateries on the blocks bordering the new lawn so they can set up patios. A meal with a view of trees is a draw in itself, and it gives merchants who fear losing car spaces a way to profit from the change.

items.label: seq_first
items.headline: Include outdoor exercise equipment for adults
items.body: Parks always have swings for kids but nothing for grown-ups. A small outdoor gym with pull-up bars, balance beams and low-impact machines would get adults and seniors exercising for free, right in the middle of downtown.

items.label: seq_second
items.headline: A free open-air workout corner
items.body: Beyond the playground, install some sturdy fitness stations: chin-up rails, stretching posts and gentle cardio devices suited to older people. Residents who can't afford a membership somewhere would have a place to stay active close to home.

items.label: seq_first
items.headline: Signs from the park to Main Street shops
items.body: Visitors who come to the park won't automatically find the stores. Put up clear signs and a map at every park entrance pointing to Main Street, with walking times and a list of the shops and restaurants. That's how the park actually turns into customers.

items.label: seq_second
items.headline: Guide park visitors toward the stores
items.body: Many newcomers to the green won't realize the retail strip is just a block away. Posted directions and a directory board at each gate, showing how many minutes on foot to the boutiques and eateries, would steer that crowd into the businesses.

items.label: seq_first
items.headline: Don't plant all one kind of tree
items.body: When the emerald ash borer came through, towns that had lined their streets with a single species lost almost all their shade in a few years. The new park should mix at least ten different tree species so one pest or disease can't wipe out the canopy.

items.label: seq_second
items.headline: Variety protects the canopy
items.body: Planting a single species is a gamble. One beetle or blight can kill every specimen, the way Dutch elm disease stripped whole neighborhoods bare. Choose a broad mix of oaks, maples, lindens and others for the green so an outbreak only takes a few.

items.label: seq_first
items.headline: Put an end date on the business levy
items.body: If downtown businesses have to pay a levy for this park, the ordinance should say the levy expires once the construction costs are covered. Too many temporary taxes quietly become permanent, and shop owners deserve to know when it stops.

items.label: seq_second
items.headline: The park charge should expire automatically
items.body: Write a sunset clause into the merchant assessment so it ends the day the project's bills are paid off. Charges sold as short-term have a habit of lingering for decades, and retailers need a firm finish line.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: shoe guy here, this hurts me
items.body: i do shoe repairs downtown. ppl basically pull up, hand me their shoes n drive off again. no garage = they go to the mall instead cos parking there costs nothing and theres always a spot

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Has anyone on council tried finding a spot mid-morning?
items.body: By ten o'clock every curb space downtown is taken. Knock the garage down and someone driving in has literally nowhere to leave the car. It's the most obvious thing to ask, and not one councillor has bothered to respond.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Lawns don't cover the lease
items.body: Talk to any shopkeeper in town and you'll hear it: shoppers have to be able to leave their cars somewhere. Grass and benches are pleasant enough, but they won't keep the landlord paid. Tear out the garage and the high street turns into an empty shell.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: They heard us plead and did it anyway
items.body: Shopkeepers along Main pleaded with the council to leave the garage standing. The response? A vote to bulldoze it. Six hundred fewer spots means fewer people through our doors and fewer people on our payrolls. Thanks for listening, folks.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Sequence matters: new garage first, then the park
items.body: I'm not against trading concrete for greenery. What worries me is wiping out every one of those spaces in one go. Put up another parking structure close by and only then bring the old one down. Do it the other way round and the stores take the hit.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Our dining room fills from that garage
items.body: Speaking as someone who runs a restaurant: our evening customers leave their cars at Elm Street night after night. Close it and our Friday and Saturday bookings are going to sink. No one is trudging half a dozen blocks through a downpour to eat out.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: RIP Main Street
items.body: Strip out that many spots and the local retailers are toast. Folks will drive out to the big shoping centres on the edge of town and thats the last we'll ever see of them.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Nowhere to walk the kids to
items.body: Honestly can't wait. We're in one of the apartment buildings in the center and there's no playground you can get to on foot. Two acres would mean my kids finally have somewhere safe to burn off energy after school.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: This is how a city center becomes a community
items.body: Open green space is the thing that makes a town center feel like a real community rather than just a district. Everybody living or working around there gets a better day-to-day life out of it.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Good riddance to the grey monstrosity
items.body: Let's be honest, that thing is a blot on the skyline. Swap it for grass, some seating and a few trees and living in the center gets a whole lot nicer.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: The garden none of us have
items.body: A huge number of us downtown rent units without so much as a patch of grass. Somewhere public like this becomes everyone's communal yard: you unwind there, you take the pup out, you bump into the folks from down the hall.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Children shouldn't only know pavement
items.body: Kids raised in the middle of town spend their childhood on blacktop. A lawn, some trees and space to run around is the least they deserve. The council got this one right.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Weekends in the new park, hear me out
items.body: Ok so hear me out. With that much room you could run a fresh produce market every single week, and then have outdoor gigs going through the warmer months. That's exactly the kind of thing that gets all of Riverton heading into the middle of town on a Saturday or Sunday, instead of everyone staying home.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Fix the craters first
items.body: Were dropping fourteen mil on a lawn when half the streets look like the surface of the moon? Somebody at city hall has got this totally upside down. Spend it on the essentails.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Kicking merchants while they're down
items.body: This so-called business levy is one more charge on stores that are hanging on by a thread. First you strip away the spaces their customers use, then you send them the bill for it. That's rubbing salt in the wound.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: What's the plan for the overrun?
items.body: I have never seen a municipal build finish at the quoted price. Say the bill lands at twenty million rather than fourteen. Does the levy climb to make up the gap? The public is owed a straight answer on that.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: 'Grant money' is still our money
items.body: Calling it state funding doesn't make it free, the public pays for it either way. I'm fond of parks, genuinely, but fourteen million is steep and I won't get behind this until I've seen an itemized breakdown of the whole budget.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Why does our park cost so much more?
items.body: Plenty of places have managed to put in parks for a small slice of that figure. Fourteen million smells padded to me, and nobody on the council has laid out what it's actually being spent on.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Downtown was a furnace
items.body: The center of town felt like an oven all through the hot months a year ago. Trade that sun-baked slab for a canopy of shade and it'll actually be survivable down there the next time a heat wave rolls in.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Basic urban heat island science
items.body: Big masses of concrete behave like a battery: they charge up with warmth during daylight and discharge it after dark. Putting tall trees in their place is among the most effective tools we have against that effect.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Think of our elderly neighbours when it's scorching
items.body: Hot spells are genuinely hard on older people, and many of them really suffer. Having a shaded green space right in the middle of town might be the difference between life and death for some of them when the temperature spikes.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: walk by it in july and tell me it's fine
items.body: seriously, stroll past that parking structure in midsummer, its radiating heat like a stovetop. put a park there and the entire area around it cools off

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: A bus ride for a cappuccino? Come on
items.body: Free transport is a lovely gesture, I'll give them that. But picture it: you leave the car way out on the edge, stand around for a bus, all so you can grab a quick coffee. I really can't see that thing getting much use.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Temporary fix, permanent problem
items.body: The shuttle only runs while the work is going on. When the diggers leave, we're still short six hundred spaces for good, and there's no bus coming to fix that.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Show us the shuttle specifics
items.body: Which lot? How frequently? For what period? Until the council puts actual answers to those on paper, 'free shuttle' is just a nice-sounding phrase.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Try juggling your shopping on a bus
items.body: Nobody's going to haul an armful of purchases up the steps of a shuttle. As a way of dealing with where shoppers leave their cars, it simply doesn't work.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Before the shovels go in, a security plan
items.body: My concern is what happens after dark. An open space with no lights and nobody keeping watch can become a magnet for criminals. I'd like the city to set out how it intends to keep people safe there before a single thing is built.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Ribbon-cuttings are easy, lawnmowers cost money
items.body: Anyone can put a park in. The hard question is who funds the grass-cutting, the litter pickup and the fixing of broken stuff year after year. Look at the state of the parks we've already got, they're neglected.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: We already know how this ends
items.body: The last green space we got in the center of town turned into a spot where people get high and hang around all day. I've got a bad feeling this new one goes the same way.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Is there money set aside for keeping it nice?
items.body: I'm genuinely keen on the idea. My hesitation is that I've watched brand-new parks go to ruin because nobody at city hall ever puts aside funds to look after them. So: is a dedicated, ongoing maintenance budget part of this or not?

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Park visitors are shoppers too
items.body: Folks who come down to spend time on the grass don't just leave afterward, they wander into the stores. The pedestrian flow around a park will do far more for the high street than that car park ever managed.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: The research favours people on foot
items.body: There's evidence that people who walk to local businesses end up spending more across a month than those who drive. More pedestrians is what a park delivers, and that means better takings for the shops.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Build for humans, not hatchbacks
items.body: Look at any thriving town center and you'll find it's somewhere you can get around on foot, with squares and green spaces. It's time Riverton quit putting vehicles first and started putting people first.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: A request on behalf of those living nearby
items.body: Removing a structure of that size will inevitably bring many months of jackhammering, airborne grit and road closures. I would respectfully ask the council to set out what measures it will take to minimise the disturbance to residents in the surrounding blocks.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Give merchants a schedule, please
items.body: Knocking the structure down will snarl the roads and throw up dirt for an extended stretch. Shop owners can cope if they know what's coming, so publish a firm timetable and let them plan around it.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Asking our opinion after the fact?
items.body: hold on, so they gave basically zero warning about the vote, and now they want feedback AFTER its done?? thats completely the wrong way round. you ask the town first, then you decide.

items.label: generic
items.headline: About time
items.body: About time the council actually did something. Glad to see it finally happening.

items.label: generic
items.headline: Who cares
items.body: Honestly I don't get why everyone is so worked up about this. Park, garage, whatever. Life goes on.

items.label: generic
items.headline: Terrible decision
items.body: This is just a bad call all round. I don't know what they were thinking.

items.label: generic
items.headline: Love it!
items.body: Great news for Riverton, love this so much. Well done everyone involved!!

items.label: generic
items.headline: Typical
items.body: Typical. Just typical. I expected nothing less from this lot.

items.label: generic
items.headline: Not sure how I feel about this
items.body: I can see it going either way honestly. Guess we'll find out in a few years.

items.label: generic
items.headline: Here we go again
items.body: Oh great, another big plan from city hall. Can't wait to see how this one turns out.

items.label: generic
items.headline: Good for them
items.body: Nice to see something new happening downtown for once. Hope it works out.

items.label: generic
items.headline: meh, whatever
items.body: meh. doesn't really affect me either way tbh

items.label: generic
items.headline: Big mistake
items.body: Mark my words, people will look back on this vote and regret it. Just a really poor choice.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Route 3 shelter still missing
items.body: The bus shelter at the Route 3 stop on Grand Avenue got knocked down by a delivery truck back in March and it still hasn't been replaced. Seniors are standing in the rain with grocery bags waiting for a bus that only comes every 40 minutes. Riverton Transit, please put something up, even a temporary bench.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: the new fare cards are a pain
items.body: tried the new tap card on the 11 this morning and the reader just beeped at me three times. driver waved me on but said half the machines dont work yet. why roll it out before its ready? also you cant load it with cash anywhere except the depot

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Makerspace at the main library is a gem
items.body: Took my teenager to the new makerspace on the second floor of the Riverton Public Library last Saturday. 3D printers, a sewing machine, a laser cutter, and staff who actually know how to use them. It's free with a library card. More people should know about this.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Later school start times, yes please
items.body: The school district wants to push the high school start from 7:25 to 8:30. As a parent of two teenagers who are basically zombies before 8, I think this is overdue. The research on teen sleep is pretty clear. My only worry is that the elementary bus runs get shuffled earlier to make it work.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Water bill up 18% and nobody explained why
items.body: Opened my quarterly water and sewer bill and it jumped 18 percent. The utility's website has one vague line about 'infrastructure investment.' If rates are going up that much, the utility board owes customers an actual breakdown of where the money is going.
items.topic: adjacent_seen: Riverton water, sewer, trash and utility rates

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Basement flooded with sewage again
items.body: Third time in two years the sewer has backed up into our basement on Linden Street after a heavy rain. The city says it's a 'combined system' problem and that a backflow valve is the homeowner's responsibility. The neighbors on both sides have had the same thing. At what point does the city own this?
items.topic: adjacent_seen: Riverton water, sewer, trash and utility rates

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Bulk pickup by appointment only now?
items.body: Next available slot is five weeks out. My old couch says hi from the porch.
items.topic: adjacent_seen: Riverton water, sewer, trash and utility rates

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Council pay raise deserves a real discussion
items.body: Buried in the consent agenda last night was a 12 percent pay increase for council members starting next year. Maybe they are underpaid, I honestly don't know, but something like that should be debated openly, not passed in one bundle with sidewalk repairs and a hydrant maintenance contract.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Drive-thru on Harlan Road is a bad fit
items.body: The planning board is hearing a request to rezone the corner of Harlan Road and 9th for a drive-through coffee chain. That intersection already backs up at school drop-off. A drive-thru line spilling onto Harlan every morning is a crash waiting to happen. I'll be at the hearing on the 14th.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Ward 4 polling place moved, check your card
items.body: Heads up, Ward 4 voters: our polling place moved from Jefferson Elementary to the Northside Community Center this year. I only noticed because I read the tiny print on the new voter card. The county clerk should really mail a separate notice, because a lot of people are going to show up at the old spot.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Millbrook's parking app is a mess
items.body: Went to Millbrook for dinner Friday and they've ripped out all the meters in favor of an app. Took me ten minutes to download it, make an account and find the zone number while my kids complained from the back seat. Nice little town, but I'm not rushing back.
items.topic: adjacent_seen: parks, garages or parking elsewhere

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Hawthorne Park tennis courts are cracked
items.body: The courts at Hawthorne Park on the east side have cracks wide enough to twist an ankle, and two of the nets have been down all summer. Our Tuesday doubles group has played there for 15 years. Could the parks department at least resurface one court before next season?
items.topic: adjacent_seen: parks, garages or parking elsewhere

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: The new pho place on Carver St is the real deal
items.body: Finally tried the pho spot that opened where the old laundromat used to be on Carver Street. The broth is rich, the portions are huge and it's under twelve bucks. Family-run and super friendly. Go on a weeknight, there was a line out the door on Saturday.
items.topic: adjacent_seen: Riverton businesses, restaurants and events

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Harvest Festival needs twice the trash cans
items.body: Loved the Riverton Harvest Festival this weekend, the apple cider donuts alone were worth it. But by Sunday afternoon every bin on the Water Street festival grounds was overflowing and there was litter along the whole fence line. Organizers, double the cans next year and add some recycling stations.
items.topic: adjacent_seen: Riverton businesses, restaurants and events

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Division Street is a slalom course
items.body: Driving Division Street between 3rd and 8th is like dodging craters. I blew a tire last week on the one by the dry cleaner, and the city's claim form says they aren't liable unless the pothole was reported first. So consider this my report. On that one and the six others. Public Works, where are you?

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Beaver Creek footbridge closed indefinitely
items.body: The footbridge on the Beaver Creek loop has had a 'closed' sign on it since the spring flooding, which cuts the trail in half. You either turn back or wade across. It's a great 5-mile hike otherwise. Does anyone know if the county has a plan or a timeline to fix it?
items.topic: adjacent_seen: nature, trails and outdoors around Riverton

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Station 3 going dark at night worries me
items.body: I heard at the neighborhood association meeting that Fire Station 3 on Kessler Road may stop staffing overnight to cut overtime costs. We live out past the rail yard and the next closest station is at least eight minutes away. Eight minutes is a long time when your kitchen is on fire. Please reconsider this.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: $1,900 for a four-mile ambulance ride
items.body: My mother fell and needed an ambulance to Riverton General. Four miles. The bill came to $1,900 and her insurance says the ambulance company is out of network. How is an emergency ride out of network?? Nobody gets to pick their ambulance. Has anyone fought one of these and won an appeal?

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Closing the maternity ward would be a disaster
items.body: Word is Riverton General is thinking about closing its labor and delivery unit and sending births to the regional hospital 45 minutes away. I delivered both my kids there. Forty-five minutes in active labor, in January, on Route 30? That is not a plan. The hospital board meets Thursday night and people should show up.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Free flu shots at the health department
items.body: Reminder that the county health department is running free flu and COVID booster clinics every Wednesday in October, 3 to 7 pm, no appointment needed. I went last week and was in and out in fifteen minutes. Bring your insurance card if you have one, but they won't turn you away if you don't.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Trap-neuter-return beats rounding up cats
items.body: Animal control wants to trap and remove the feral cat colonies behind the shopping plazas. That's been tried in plenty of places and the colonies just refill. A trap-neuter-return program run with local volunteers costs less and actually shrinks the population within a few years. I volunteer with a TNR group and we'd be glad to help.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Coyote took our neighbor's cat
items.body: A warning for folks on the north side near the golf course. We've seen a coyote three evenings this week, and on Monday it grabbed our neighbor's cat right off their deck. Keep small pets inside at dusk and don't leave food out. Animal control says there isn't much they can do.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: State gas tax hike hits rural commuters hardest
items.body: The legislature's proposed 9-cent gas tax increase sounds small, but for people in our part of the state who drive 40 miles each way to work, it adds up to hundreds of dollars a year. I get that the bridges need fixing. Tie it to income or offer a commuter credit instead of raising it across the board.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: A shutdown would hit federal workers here too
items.body: People forget how many federal employees live around Riverton, between the VA clinic, the postal distribution center and the Army Corps field office. If Congress lets the government shut down again next month, those families miss paychecks, and it ripples out to every landlord and diner that depends on them. I don't care which party blinks first. Call your representative and tell them to pass a budget. Last time my neighbor went five weeks without pay and had to borrow from her parents to cover the mortgage.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: What a comeback for the girls soccer team!
items.body: Down 1-0 with six minutes left Friday night and the Riverton High girls scored twice to beat Westfield and head to the state semifinals. Maya Ortiz's header off the corner kick was unbelievable. The bleachers were packed. Semifinal is Tuesday at 6, and the fan bus leaves the school at 3.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Coed softball league needs two more teams
items.body: The Thursday night coed softball league is short two teams for spring, so we might end up with a shorter schedule. It's $40 a player, bring your own glove, and skill ranges from ex-college players to me (not good). Message the league's Facebook page if you can pull a team together.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Four days without power after the windstorm
items.body: We lost power Saturday night when the windstorm came through and didn't get it back until Wednesday. The outage map said 'estimated restoration: assessing' the whole time. I know crews were stretched thin, but a real update or two would have helped. We lost a full freezer of food.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Hail dented half the cars on our street
items.body: That hail on Tuesday afternoon was golf ball sized for about five minutes. Dented hoods, a cracked windshield next door, and now our skylight leaks. If you're filing claims, take photos before anything gets moved, and be careful with the roofers going door to door who aren't licensed in this state.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Ashford County's food scrap pickup works
items.body: My sister lives over in Ashford County, and they started curbside food scrap collection two years ago. Every house got a small green bin, it all goes to a compost facility, and their landfill tonnage dropped by about a fifth. Not perfect, the fruit flies in August are real, but it seems to be working.
items.topic: adjacent_unseen: recycling and environmental policy elsewhere

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Bottle deposit laws actually work
items.body: Having lived in Michigan, I can tell you a 10-cent deposit on cans and bottles changes behavior almost overnight. You basically never see cans in ditches there, because somebody always picks them up for the dime. States without a deposit law should stop debating it and just copy one.
items.topic: adjacent_unseen: recycling and environmental policy elsewhere

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: The mill exhibit at the history museum
items.body: The Riverton Historical Society museum just opened an exhibit on the old textile mill: photos of the 1912 strike, a loom you can actually operate, and recorded interviews with women who worked there in the 1950s. My grandfather worked the night shift there. I spent two hours and could have stayed longer. Admission is $5.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Riverton Players' Our Town was wonderful
items.body: saw the community theater's production of Our Town at the high school auditorium last night and honestly teared up in act three. the guy playing the stage manager was perfect. only two more shows this weekend and there were lots of empty seats, so go! tickets are $15, $8 for students

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Why is my sourdough so flat?
items.body: Third loaf this month that spreads out like a pancake in the oven. My starter doubles in about 6 hours, I'm at 75% hydration with bread flour and an overnight cold proof. Is it my shaping? Should I drop the hydration? Any bakers out there with tips?

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Finally read Project Hail Mary and get the hype
items.body: The science is surprisingly careful, the friendship at the center of it is genuinely moving, and I laughed out loud more than once. People say the audiobook is even better. What should I read next if I liked this?

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Laptop loses 30% battery overnight
items.body: My laptop drops about 30% overnight with the lid closed. I already turned off wake timers and Bluetooth. Is this just how modern standby works or is the battery dying? It's about two years old.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Lisbon in November is worth it
items.body: Just got back from ten days in Portugal. Lisbon in November was mild, around 60 degrees, and the crowds were a fraction of summer. Ride the 28 tram early before the tour groups, get your pasteis de nata warm, and give Sintra a full day, not half. Honestly Porto was even better.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: The London System is boring but it works
items.body: Everyone online mocks the London, but I went from 1100 to 1450 in six months just by playing it every game as white and learning the middlegame plans instead of memorizing lines. Being bored is fine if you're winning.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Autodraft gave me two kickers
items.body: My laptop died mid-draft and I came back to a roster with two kickers, three tight ends and zero running backs after round four. Is there any saving this season or do I start trading everything for RBs right now?

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: fiddle leaf fig dropping leaves
items.body: mine has dropped 6 leaves in 2 weeks since i moved it away from the window. brown spots on the edges too. watering once a week. is it the light, the water, or is it just being dramatic like everyone says they do

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Those new deep field images are unreal
items.body: The latest telescope images of distant galaxy clusters are stunning. Some of that light left its source more than 13 billion years ago. Puts everyday worries in perspective. Does anyone know a good explainer on how they choose the colors, since it's infrared and not what our eyes would see?

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: The secret to good chili is time
items.body: Brown the meat in batches, bloom the spices in the fat, add a square of dark chocolate and a splash of coffee, then leave it on the lowest heat for three hours. Beans optional, argue amongst yourselves. Always better the next day.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Beat the final boss after 40 tries
items.body: Took me an entire weekend but I finally beat the last boss of the Elden Ring DLC. Switched to a bleed build and stopped panic rolling. My hands are still shaking. If you're stuck, summon the NPC helper, no shame in it.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Thank you to whoever turned in my wallet
items.body: I dropped my wallet somewhere between the bank and my car after parking downtown on Thursday. Someone turned it in at the police front desk with every card and even the forty dollars still inside. Whoever you are, thank you. You restored a little of my faith in people.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Wedding photographer recommendations?
items.body: We're getting married next June and want outdoor photos, maybe at Lakeside Park or down by the river. Looking for a local photographer who's good with natural light and under about $3,000. Bonus points if they can wrangle a very large, very loud Italian family. Any names you'd recommend?

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Council livestream audio is unlistenable
items.body: I've tried to watch the last few council meetings online and could barely hear a thing. Half the microphones were off and the other half buzzed. I'm not following any one issue, I just like to know what's going on in town. Can the city clerk get the AV system fixed? It can't cost that much.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Car broken into at the grocery store
items.body: Someone smashed my passenger window in the FreshMart parking lot on Route 9 around 6pm on a Sunday, in broad daylight, and took a gym bag. Police said there have been several like it this month. Don't leave anything visible in your car, not even an empty bag.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Best running shoes for flat feet?
items.body: I've started running again, mostly early morning loops around the park near my apartment, and my arches are killing me after about two miles. The guy at the store suggested stability shoes. Anyone with flat feet have a pair they swear by? Budget is around $140.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Looking for a dentist downtown
items.body: Just moved to Riverton for a new job and need a dentist, ideally somewhere downtown near my office so I can go on a lunch break. My last dentist was very patient with a nervous patient (me). Anyone have someone they love? My insurance is Delta if that helps.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Night-shift nurses rely on that garage
items.body: St. Mary's Hospital is two blocks away and has no staff lot of its own. Nurses coming off a 3am shift walk to the Elm Street garage because it is lit and staffed. A remote shuttle lot at that hour is not a safe option for them.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Test the soil before promising a park
items.body: Fifty years of oil drips, and possibly an old fuel tank under the ramp, mean the ground may be contaminated. Environmental cleanup can easily add millions, and I see no line for soil remediation in the $14 million estimate.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Make part of the lawn a winter ice rink
items.body: Most parks sit empty from November to March. If one flat section of the new park were designed to be flooded as a public skating rink each winter, downtown would have a reason for people to visit in the cold months too.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Price the street spots instead of keeping them free
items.body: The real problem is that curb spaces on Main Street are free, so employees park in them all day. Meters with demand-based pricing would keep one or two spaces open on every block for customers, which matters more than the garage count.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Line one edge of the site with affordable homes
items.body: Two acres is big enough to set aside a narrow strip along the north edge for a row of affordable apartments. People living right beside the park would become everyday customers for Main Street, which answers the shop owners better than any garage.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Use the demolition to train local apprentices
items.body: The council should require the demolition and landscaping contractors to take on apprentices from Riverton Technical College. A $14 million public job could leave behind skilled local workers, not just grass.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Where will the plows dump downtown snow?
items.body: Every winter the public works crews pile snow cleared from downtown streets onto the garage roof deck. Once the garage is gone there is no obvious place for it, and snowbanks will eat the very street parking shops depend on.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Crush the old concrete into the park's paths
items.body: Instead of trucking the demolished decks to a landfill, the rubble can be crushed on site and reused as the base for the walking paths and the playground foundation. That cuts hundreds of truck trips through downtown and lowers the demolition bill.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Capture the rise in property values instead of a levy
items.body: Buildings facing a new park usually gain value. Rather than a flat levy on every downtown business, the city could fund the project from the added property tax on the blocks around the park, so those who benefit most pay most.

items.label: novel
items.headline: A memory garden for the care home residents
items.body: The Maple Court care home is across the street from the garage. A small enclosed sensory garden with raised planters and scented herbs would let residents with dementia spend time outdoors safely, something they cannot do now.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Demolish in January, not before the holidays
items.body: Retailers make a third of their annual sales between Thanksgiving and New Year. The contract should forbid starting demolition until after the holiday season, so the loudest, dustiest months fall in the slowest weeks of the retail year.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Our supper crowd will vanish
items.body: I own a bistro on Elm. Most evening diners leave their car in that garage and walk over. Take it away and nobody is hiking half a mile in a downpour for pasta, so our Friday and Saturday bookings will fall off.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Nice priorities, council
items.body: Sure, spend fourteen million on flower beds while my street has potholes you could lose a tire in. Fix the roads and the basics first, then talk to me about parks.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Concrete stores heat, trees release it
items.body: A multi-level concrete structure absorbs solar radiation during the day and radiates it back after sunset, keeping the surrounding blocks warm overnight. Replacing it with a canopy of mature trees is a proven way to reduce the urban heat island.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Seen this movie before
items.body: The last park we built downtown turned into a place for dealers and people sleeping on benches. I expect the same thing here.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Consultation should precede the vote
items.body: It is troubling that the council gave so little notice of this vote and opened public comment only once the decision had already been made. Residents ought to have been heard before the council acted, not afterwards.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: A shared yard for apartment dwellers
items.body: Most of us downtown live in flats without a scrap of lawn. This park would be the backyard we all share, somewhere to unwind, take the dog out and actually get to know the people next door.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Who rides a bus for a latte?
items.body: Nice that the shuttle is free, but honestly, who is going to leave their car at some far lot and wait around for a bus just to pick up a coffee downtown? I can't see many people using it.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Walkers outspend drivers
items.body: Research keeps finding that people on foot spend more at neighborhood stores over a month than people who drive in. A park will bring more pedestrians downtown, and that is good for sales.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: construction is gonna be awful
items.body: tearing down a giant concrete garage = months of jackhammers, dust everywhere and streets closed. council needs to tell us how theyre going to keep the mess down for people who live nearby

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Who will take care of park after
items.body: To build the park is easy part. But who is paying for cut the grass, clean and fix it every year? The parks we have already are not maintained good.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Pay a tax to lose your own customers
items.body: Let me get this straight: downtown shops get charged a new levy, and the money pays for a park that eliminates the parking our customers use. That is ridiculous and the levy has to go.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Perfect spot for a Saturday market
items.body: Two acres downtown would make a great home for a weekly farmers market and some outdoor music in the summer. That would pull the whole town into the center on weekends.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: The river trail wildflowers are out
items.body: The trail along the river north of Riverton is covered in wildflowers right now. We saw herons, a family of otters and some beautiful old oak trees. Bring water, it gets hot in the afternoon.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Riverton River Cats clinch the pennant
items.body: Our minor league baseball team finally won the division. The pitching staff was lights out all September and the stadium was packed for the final home game. Great summer for local baseball.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Library branch hours cut again
items.body: The Eastside branch library is now closed on Mondays and Wednesdays. Students who rely on the computers after school have nowhere else to go. The city should restore the staff funding.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Water main break flooded Oak Avenue
items.body: Another water main burst on Oak Avenue this morning and the road was closed for hours. These pipes are nearly a hundred years old and the utility keeps patching instead of replacing them.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Community garden plots available
items.body: The allotment behind the church on Pine Street has three open plots this season. Raised beds, compost and water are provided, and the tomatoes there grow better than anywhere I have tried.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Highway 12 roadwork is a mess
items.body: The lane closures on Highway 12 have doubled my commute to the office park. The state transportation department promised the work would be finished by August and it is still going.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: School board should not cut music
items.body: The school board is voting next week on cutting the middle school music program to save money. Music teaches discipline and teamwork, and kids who play instruments do better in math.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Camping trip to Pine Ridge State Park
items.body: We spent three nights at Pine Ridge State Park last weekend. The campsites by the lake are shaded by tall pines, the hiking loop is well marked and the rangers were very helpful.

items.label: tricky
items.headline: Is there asbestos in the garage?
items.body: Garages built in the early 1970s often used asbestos in the fireproofing and pipe insulation. Has anyone surveyed the structure? Safe removal would change the demolition timeline and the cost.

items.label: tricky
items.headline: What about monthly pass holders?
items.body: Hundreds of people pay for monthly garage permits. Will they get refunds or reserved spots at the outer lot?

items.label: tricky
items.headline: Same council, still no streetlights
items.body: The council that just voted for this park still has not repaired the broken streetlights on my block in Eastside after two years of complaints. Fix the neighborhoods you already have before starting new projects.

items.label: tricky
items.headline: Too costly and bad for shops
items.body: Spending fourteen million dollars is excessive for what is basically a lawn. Worse, without the garage people will not be able to park near the stores and Main Street will lose its customers to the malls.

items.label: tricky
items.headline: Some thoughts on the park
items.body: Kids downtown need a place to play. The price tag is steep. Shops will miss the parking. The council should also ask the transit authority to move the Route 4 bus terminal onto the park's edge, so people can arrive without a car.

items.label: tricky
items.headline: Riverton needs a skate park by the river
items.body: Teenagers in Riverton have nowhere to skate. The empty lot beside the boat launch on the east bank would be perfect for a concrete skate bowl and some ramps, and it is far from any houses.

items.label: tricky
items.headline: The shop owners have it backwards
items.body: Merchants keep saying the park will cost them customers, but a busy park is exactly what brings people downtown. Visitors who come for the green space will stop in the stores on their way, so Main Street will gain shoppers, not lose them.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Route 7 bus cuts hurt commuters
items.body: Riverton Transit is dropping evening service on Route 7 after 8pm. People who work late shifts at the warehouse district now have no way home except expensive taxis.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Police department is short staffed
items.body: The Riverton police chief told the council the department is down eleven officers. Response times on the west side have doubled, and the city needs to fund recruitment bonuses.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: My property assessment jumped 30 percent
items.body: The county reassessed every home in Riverton this year and mine went up thirty percent. Retirees on fixed incomes cannot absorb tax bills like this, and the appeal process is confusing.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: West side housing tower is overdue
items.body: The planning board approved a 200-unit affordable housing tower near the old mill on the west side. Rents in Riverton have climbed for years and young families are being priced out.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Recycling pickup every other week is not enough
items.body: Since the city switched recycling collection to every two weeks, our bins overflow and cardboard blows all over the street. The savings are not worth the mess.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Who is running for mayor?
items.body: The mayoral election is in November and I still know almost nothing about the candidates. The local paper should host a debate so residents can compare their platforms.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: The fairgrounds market is worth the drive
items.body: The Sunday market at the county fairgrounds has grown to over sixty vendors. The honey stand and the Mexican bakery are my favorites, and there is plenty of room to walk around.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Fifth Street dog run needs a better fence
items.body: The fence at the Fifth Street dog run has a gap near the gate and small dogs keep slipping out into traffic. Parks staff have been told three times and nothing has been repaired.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Quick-stop trade depends on parking
items.body: I mend boots and heels downtown. Nearly everybody pulls up, hands me a pair, and heads off again. Remove those bays and they'll simply take their errands to the shopping center with its easy free lot.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Apartment kids have no swings nearby
items.body: If you live in a downtown flat there isn't a single playground you can reach on foot. This two-acre green would give parents like me somewhere secure for the children once school lets out.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Dark parks invite trouble
items.body: My concern is that after sunset the lawn could draw criminal activity unless it is properly illuminated and policed. Before construction starts the city should present a security strategy.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: What happens when the budget blows up?
items.body: Government construction almost never comes in on budget. Suppose the final bill is twenty million rather than fourteen: does the business levy rise to cover it? We deserve to know now.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: A temporary bus is not a fix
items.body: Running a shuttle while the work is underway helps for a year or two at most. When the ribbon is cut, downtown will still be permanently missing six hundred places to leave a car.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Goodbye to a concrete blight
items.body: That parking structure is hideous. Swapping it for lawns, shade and some benches will make living downtown far nicer.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Elderly residents need shade
items.body: Hot summers are dangerous for older people. Having a tree-covered park in the middle of town could genuinely prevent deaths when temperatures spike.

items.label: paraphrase
items.headline: Design downtown for pedestrians
items.body: The downtowns that flourish are the ones you can explore on foot, full of squares and green space. Riverton should quit planning around automobiles and begin planning around residents.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Wait until after Christmas to tear it down
items.body: Shops on Main Street depend on the November and December rush. The council should schedule the demolition of the garage for January so the construction noise and closed streets do not wipe out their busiest weeks.

items.label: novel
items.headline: Timing of the demolition matters
items.body: Please do not start knocking down the Elm Street garage in the fall. Losing the parking during holiday shopping season would hit downtown stores hardest, so begin the work in the quiet months after New Year.

items.label: novel
items.headline: No demolition during holiday shopping
items.body: If the garage comes down in November, Main Street merchants lose their parking right when holiday sales matter most. Put a clause in the contract that demolition cannot begin until after the holidays.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Keep the library open on weekends
items.body: The main library has stopped opening on Saturdays because of budget cuts. Parents who work weekdays have lost the only time they could bring their kids to borrow books.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Fund the libraries properly
items.body: Cutting library hours saves the city a tiny amount of money but takes away free internet, homework help and a warm place for people with nowhere else to go.

items.label: off_topic
items.headline: Great new librarian at the Eastside branch
items.body: The new children's librarian at the Eastside branch started a Tuesday story hour and it is always full. My daughter now asks to go to the library every week.
